why: The new examples shifted the model toward making earlier cuts in many short/medium spans (it began inserting cuts between auxiliaries/short verbs and their objects and even inside noun phrases), producing large negative moves on examples that were split inside NPs or that separated verb+argument; at the same time the reporting-verb example improved handling of enumerations and some medium-length predicate groupings, which matches the positive deltas in the ≤5 and ≤7 bins.
lesson: Keep the reporting-verb example that helped medium-length predicate/enumeration splits, but avoid examples or placements that encourage premature cuts inside noun phrases or between auxiliaries and their complements.
